format.vectors: rules (the agent's redact block format: a custom rule has name, pattern, secret_group and max_length, the longest match it can make in bytes; the guard before the cut of a long line is the largest of cut_guard_bytes and the max_length of every custom rule), input or input_b64 (input_encoding encodes input: utf-8 by default, utf-16-le or utf-16-be), source_encoding (none: bytes; auto: detected from the first 64 bytes; utf-16-le; utf-16-be; utf-16-unsure: served as bytes, the detectors run on the bytes and on the UTF-16 LE and BE readings aligned on even file offsets, and the union is replaced), output_encoding (utf-8 by default, or source), final (true by default), max_line_bytes, pem_max_lines; expected or expected_b64 (expected_encoding like input_encoding), counts, source_offset, trailing_partial, or error. A vector with window redacts input[window.start:] of a read that began window.base_offset bytes into the file, and expects begin, end and aligned. Every vector without window must give the same result whatever block sizes the input is fed in. refused_at and union_at, when present, are where a line that looks UTF-32 made the rest refused and where the content started to be read as utf-16-unsure part way (offsets into input), or null for neither.
format.long_line_cuts:
for every k from 0 to the length of value, the line kept + ' ' + '~' * n + ' ' + value + ' end
', with n such that max_line_bytes falls right after the first k bytes of value, is redacted with rules and max_line_bytes and must give expected_kept (followed by ' ' and the '~' filler when the blank just before value is at or before max_line_bytes - cut_guard_bytes), the long-line marker and '
', with counts, whatever block sizes it is fed in: the kept start of a long line ends at the last blank at or before max_line_bytes - cut_guard_bytes (detectors.json), or earlier at the start of a replacement that blank would cut, so nothing of a value cut by the limit is kept. With source_encoding utf-16-unsure, the line is encoded with input_encoding (utf-16-le or utf-16-be) and redacted as utf-16-unsure from file offset 0: k and n count characters, the guard is 2 * cut_guard_bytes source bytes (a character of the UTF-16 readings takes two), the blanks are found byte by byte (the 0x20 of '20 00' and of '00 20'), and the kept start ends at the blank's 0x20 byte; the expected output is expected_kept encoded with input_encoding except its markers, which stay ASCII, then the ' ' and '~' filler encoded likewise when kept, then for utf-16-be the 00 byte before the blank's 0x20, then the long-line marker and '
' in ASCII, then for utf-16-le the 00 byte that follows the line's 0x0A.
format.head_digests: HMAC-SHA256 with key_b64 of the first min(64, offset) bytes of data, hex, first 32 characters.
format.detect: the encoding decided from head_b64: utf-16-le, utf-16-be, utf-16-unsure, null (bytes) or error.
format.rule_digests: rules_digest of rules: the SHA-256 of their canonical JSON (keys sorted, no spaces, non-ASCII characters as they are), hex.
format.rule_errors: rule lists both engines refuse to compile (a rule error), unless accepted is true, which marks a limit both engines accept; message, when present, is how the error message ends in both engines (each starts it with the rule's name).
format.generated: vectors named generated come from random content redacted by the Python engine (reviewed when they change); vectors named parity pin where RE2, in Latin-1 or UTF-8, and Go's regexp could part.
